edges.description: Reduced MCC activity blocks normal leucine-catabolic flux and diverts upstream carbon into characteristic organic acids and C5OH acylcarnitine.
Formation and excretion of hydroxyisovalerylcarnitine is associated with depletion of free carnitine in a subset of affected people.
In a minority, infection or another catabolic stress coincides with an organic-aciduria-like crisis; the factors separating tolerant from vulnerable individuals remain unknown.
Cell and tissue-preparation experiments suggest that chronic metabolite exposure may perturb mitochondrial and redox homeostasis, but this has not been shown to cause human symptoms.
Organic-aciduria-like decompensation can produce metabolic acidosis.
Mild hyperammonemia can accompany severe biochemical decompensation.
Vomiting can be an early clinical manifestation of acute crisis.
Seizures can occur during severe acute decompensation.
Severe decompensation can progress to coma.
